items.title: 变体假名隐写
items.text: 术语 ：变体假名隐写（Variant Kana Steganography）。变体假名隐写利用日语假名异体字的细微差别承载信息：不同写法代表不同比特，表面文本仍可读。它属于文本隐写，依赖排版和字体支持，数字化后容易被归一化破坏。 该条目单列，是因为它把破译方法中的术语落到可核证据：有可指认的参与者、可复算的步骤，或有馆藏、档案、标准编号支撑的实物与文本。相邻条目只用于定位，不并入该条目，也不替别条作证明。 用途描述只回答“它解决什么问题、在什么场景出现”；具体参数、协议流程与实现细节见对应算法或协议条目。 边界失效发生在三种情况：外延被同义词偷偷扩大、翻译版本改变定义、相邻概念被当作同一对象。出现其中一种，术语判断就不再可靠。 本目录把它放在前沿（e18-frontier）与基础与术语（d01-foundations）的交叉位置。具体年代、人物与版本仍需按原始来源逐项核验。 定义、正例与反例 变体假名隐写利用日语假名异体字的细微差别承载信息：不同写法代表不同比特，表面文本仍可读。它属于文本隐写，依赖排版和字体支持，数字化后容易被归一化破坏。 正例必须落在外延内；反例必须刚好跨过边界，说明它缺哪一个必要条件，而不是只给同义词。 没有标准定义时用权威教材，但仍标出版本与适用范围；术语条目不以“大家都知道”作为定义依据。 与相邻概念的辨析 变体假名隐写与相邻术语的区别不在名称，而在定义域与判据：前者要求哪些必要条件、排除哪些对象、在哪个标准或教材中有定义。 辨析时先找上位概念，再找区别特征，最后给反例；只给同义词或英文缩写不算定义。若两个术语在文献中混用，正文并列保留差异，不强行合并。 形式化记录 把 变体假名隐写 记作对象 X，定义域 D、值域 R、判据 P。若 P(x)=1，则 x 属于 X；若 P(x)=0，则不属于。判据必须可观察，不能写成“大家都知道”。 形式化只覆盖定义层；具体算法、协议或器件的安全性另见对应条目。术语条目不替算法证明，也不把数学记号当成历史证据。 - Wikipedia search entry for 变体假名隐写. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E5%8F%98%E4%BD%93%E5%81%87%E5%90%8D%E9%9A%90%E5%86%99 - RFC 4949: Internet Security Glossary, Version 2. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4949 定义检查模型 上位概念 → 区别特征 → 正例 → 反例 → 易混边界。正例必须落在外延内；反例必须刚好跨过边界；同义词不能代替定义。

items.title: VENONA 片段
items.text: 器物 ：VENONA 片段（VENONA Fragment）。 实物/文献 ：VENONA 片段（VENONA Fragment）。1943 年起，美国陆军信号情报机构截获苏联驻美机构的外交电报，代号 VENONA。破译员利用一次性密码本被违规复用的致命失误，持续解密近四十年，撕开了剑桥五杰与罗森伯格夫妇等冷战间谍网。以下为破译电文的史料化节选（代号为原档所载）。档案坐标：密件册 · 1943-80 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： venona 。该条目只陈述项目档案中可核的实物或文献信息，不把展签、网络转述或复制品当成原件。 这份材料值得保留，是因为它把抽象的密码学问题落到一个可观察的对象上：「[我们]毫不怀疑……TANGER 已抵达新的任职地点。……他沉寂已久，如今重新开始工作。……他的妻子同在这一[项]工作之中。……所有材料均已按计划移交，其余细节待下次电报确认。」（史料化节选·仿 VENONA 原档文体转写，非逐字原文） 🤔 反事实思考：如果苏联严格遵循一次性密码本的规则——绝不复用任何一页——VENONA 项目将永远不会存在，罗森伯格夫妇可能不会上电椅，冷战的间谍战场将是一片真正的黑暗。一个操作员的失误，照亮了整个地下世界。它的价值在于提供问题入口，而不是替所有相关谜题给出答案。 阅读这件器物时，抓住三个问题：谁持有或操作它、它把什么结构约束变成可验证的步骤、失败时留下什么可见证据。实物参数只写馆藏、铭文或档案能支持的数值。 该器物本身不构成安全系统；原件、复制品与复原模型混用，铭文误读，或缺少馆藏记录时，不能据此推断年代、作者或用途。 密件册 · 1943-80 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： venona 。1943 年起，美国陆军信号情报机构截获苏联驻美机构的外交电报，代号 VENONA。 物证模型与不确定性 VENONA 片段按输入（尺寸、材质、铭文、结构或操作记录）—结构（可见部件与连接关系）—操作（同时代的使用方式）—证据（馆藏、档案、铭文或技术手册）阅读。来源链包括：Wikipedia search entry for VENONA 片段；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights；Museum/collection record for VENONA 片段。 原件、复制品、复原模型和照片必须分开；年代、作者、用途、铭文读法有争议时并列保留；没有馆藏或档案支持的参数不写成确定值。 同名概念的分界 VENONA 片段只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for VENONA 片段（Tier 3）；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights（Tier 1）；Museum/collection record for VENONA 片段（Tier 1）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 读法：从对象到证据 读 VENONA 片段 先固定对象：它是什么类型、属于应用安全工程的哪一段、与哪些条目相邻。再列证据：谁在何时说了什么、locator 在哪、是否为一手材料。最后写边界：哪些结论只是模型关系，哪些仍待核。 不要把目录位置当参数表，不要把标题当定理，也不要把一次示例当普适结论；这三类是该条目明确拒绝的误读。 复核清单 检查 VENONA 片段 时逐项回答：对象类型是否固定；时间、地点、参与者是否各有来源；文本、器物或机构记录是否区分一手与二手；相邻条目是否被误并；没有来源的空白是否明确留空。五项中任何一项只能靠猜测，就停在“待核”，不把叙事写成证明。 - items.title: VENONA 破译
items.text: 攻击 ：VENONA 破译（VENONA Cryptanalysis）。 码本 + 一次性密码本 苏联商务、外交与情报电文先查码本得 x_i，再用一次性密码本 k_i 逐位模 10 相加： c_i=(x_i+k_i) mod 10。若 k_i 真随机、只使用一次且与 x_i 等长，则密文对消息是完美保密的；VENONA 的突破口不是算法，而是密码本页被重复使用。 复用与深度 c_i⊖c_i′=(x_i⊖x_i′) mod 10。掩码被消去，剩下两个码本码组的差。重复页越多、消息越长，深度越大；分析者再借助码本频率、已知片段和英文/俄文 crib，恢复码组含义并翻译。 VENONA 证明一次性密码本的安全条件是不可重复使用。它把“密钥复用”从抽象禁忌变成可操作的历史案例：一旦复用，OTP 就退化为可统计分析的 running-key 问题。JN-25 的加法簿本来就会重复使用；VENONA 的 OTP 本应只用一次，却因约 35,000 页重复制造出深度。两者的制度背景与失效性质不同，不能都写成“加法簿复用”。 1.找重复页：用相同位置的密文序列匹配，定位同一页。2.对齐消息，逐位相减得到码本差分。3.用 depth、频率和 crib 恢复码组。4.反查码本，得到明文；对仍不通的片段做语言猜测。5.记录覆盖率和翻译置信度。 不能怎么用 不能把部分解密说成完整原文；不能忽略码本更换和抄收错误；不能把 VENONA 的结果当作 OTP 算法本身可破。 1.正确使用 OTP 时无解：密钥真随机、不重复、不短于消息，VENONA 方法失效。2.复用页稀少：约 35,000 页重复密钥相对巨量流量仍是少数；只有部分电文可读。3.码本更换/编译错误：码组含义变化会产生系统性误读。4.翻译瓶颈：即使码组恢复，人名、缩写和俄语语法仍可能误判；不能把部分解密当成完整原文。 1943 年 2 月，美国陆军信号情报局启动后来代号 VENONA 的秘密项目；1945 年出现深度线索，1946 年 2 月由 Meredith Gardner 读出首条消息；项目持续到 1980 年 10 月。1995 年 7 月起分六批公开约 3,000 条翻译。公开资料确认约 35,000 页重复密钥，但并非所有重复页都可利用；该条目只写机制、规模与已公开的时间线，不把情报史结论扩大为密码学定理。 技术参数与复算边界 该条目的形式模型是 \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\mathrm{attack}}_A(\lambda)=\Pr[\mathrm{Game}_A(\lambda)=1]-\frac12\)。输入：输入：VENONA 破译的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：λ 安全参数；Game 把攻击目标写成挑战-响应游戏。 预期输出：按 VENONA 破译 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。 复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。 参数与状态规模 公式 \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\mathrm{attack}}_A(\lambda)=\Pr[\mathrm{Game}_A(\lambda)=1]-\frac12\) 的输入、输出和单位必须逐项登记；复算顺序为：1. 定义挑战与获胜条件 2. 给攻击者 oracle 访问 3. 计算优势并与目标界比较。 状态规模、密钥长度、分组长度和轮数决定复杂度；这些量不能从标题推断，必须以标准或实现文档为准。 测试向量与实现边界 标准测试向量只证明某组输入在某个实现中产生了预期输出，不证明所有参数都安全。记录测试向量时至少要写：算法/模式、密钥、明文或消息、随机数/IV、输出长度、实现版本。该条目已登记的限制是：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。 如果实现使用查表、分支或可变时间操作，算法层的证明不能替代侧信道评估；如果协议层没有认证，算法层的机密性也不能阻止替换或重放。 - items.title: 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚
items.text: 人物 ：布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚（Blaise de Vigenère）。布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚是法国外交官与密码学家。他出身外交世家，青年时出使罗马，在教廷钻研大量密码文献。1586 年，他出版《密码论》，系统整理并推广多表替换思想，还独创了「自动密钥」密码——让明文字母自身延伸为密钥。虽然这套方案的核心思想源自意大利人贝拉索，19 世纪起它却被冠以维吉尼亚之名，成为西方密码史上最著名的「不可破译的密码」，直到 1863 年才被卡西斯基攻破。 冷知识：维吉尼亚晚年痴迷炼金术与神秘学，《密码论》出版时他已年过六旬——密码学只是这位外交官多彩人生的晚年一章，却成了他身后最响亮的名字。保留这一人物条目的理由，是它能把一个具体的人与其时代、工作和相邻实体区分开；人物影响不自动等于其个人独力完成的结果。 「一个字母，可以换二十六副面孔。（意译，编者拟）」 这句话用于标识该人物在资料中的立场或表述，不把它当成制度性结论，也不把后世引用当成原始史料。 人物条目的边界：史料有限，纪念性说法、归属争议和后世追认都要与可核生平分开。不把集体成果、同名算法或同名事件自动归到本人；不把一句名言当成其全部思想。 可核角色与证据链 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚归入基础与术语，登记时代为文艺复兴与宗教改革。该条目只登记有来源支持的教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件与可核同行评价。来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews；MacTutor biography: Blaise de Vigenère。 没有来源支持的出生、死亡、家庭、师承、奖项、论文数量和任职日期不补写；同名人物不合并；后人归功与本人文本分开。 同名概念的分界 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚（Tier 3）；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews（Tier 2）；MacTutor biography: Blaise de Vigenère（Tier 2）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 - Wikipedia search entry for 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E5%B8%83%E8%8E%B1%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E5%BE%B7%C2%B7%E7%BB%B4%E5%90%89%E5%B0%BC%E4%BA%9A - MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews. https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/ - MacTutor biography: Blaise de Vigenère. https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Vigenere/ 角色关系模型 只登记四类关系：教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件、可核同行评价。每条关系都要有来源；没有来源的师承、奖项和私生活不进入模型。

items.text: 人物 ：查尔斯·惠斯通（Charles Wheatstone）。惠斯通是维多利亚时代的科学全才：与库克合作发明实用电报，推广了以他命名的电桥，还痴迷于用机器藏信。1854 年他发明 Playfair 密码——把明文按字母两两分组，用 5×5 方阵整体加密，单字母的频率统计从此失效。它由好友莱昂·普莱费尔引荐给军方并冠名，后被英军用于布尔战争与一战，成为「双字母加密」的经典范本。 冷知识：他名下最出名的两样东西其实都不「属于」他——Playfair 密码以推广者普莱费尔命名，惠斯通电桥的真正发明者是克里斯蒂；倒是那台用偏振光传送密文的「惠斯通密码机」，才是他亲手造的原汁原味发明。保留这一人物条目的理由，是它能把一个具体的人与其时代、工作和相邻实体区分开；人物影响不自动等于其个人独力完成的结果。 「「让字母两两起舞，单字母的频率统计就失去了准头。」（概括 Playfair 密码的设计思想）」 这句话用于标识该人物在资料中的立场或表述，不把它当成制度性结论，也不把后世引用当成原始史料。 人物条目的边界：史料有限，纪念性说法、归属争议和后世追认都要与可核生平分开。不把集体成果、同名算法或同名事件自动归到本人；不把一句名言当成其全部思想。 可核角色与证据链 查尔斯·惠斯通归入基础与术语，登记时代为第一次世界大战。该条目只登记有来源支持的教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件与可核同行评价。来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 查尔斯·惠斯通；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews。 没有来源支持的出生、死亡、家庭、师承、奖项、论文数量和任职日期不补写；同名人物不合并；后人归功与本人文本分开。 同名概念的分界 查尔斯·惠斯通只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 查尔斯·惠斯通（Tier 3）；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews（Tier 2）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 读法：从对象到证据 读 查尔斯·惠斯通 先固定对象：它是什么类型、属于基础与术语的哪一段、与哪些条目相邻。再列证据：谁在何时说了什么、locator 在哪、是否为一手材料。最后写边界：哪些结论只是模型关系，哪些仍待核。 不要把目录位置当参数表，不要把标题当定理，也不要把一次示例当普适结论；这三类是该条目明确拒绝的误读。 复核清单 检查 查尔斯·惠斯通 时逐项回答：对象类型是否固定；时间、地点、参与者是否各有来源；文本、器物或机构记录是否区分一手与二手；相邻条目是否被误并；没有来源的空白是否明确留空。五项中任何一项只能靠猜测，就停在“待核”，不把叙事写成证明。 - Wikipedia search entry for 查尔斯·惠斯通. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E6%9F%A5%E5%B0%94%E6%96%AF%C2%B7%E6%83%A0%E6%96%AF%E9%80%9A - MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews. https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/ 角色关系模型 只登记四类关系：教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件、可核同行评价。每条关系都要有来源；没有来源的师承、奖项和私生活不进入模型。

items.title: Whirlpool 512 位散列
items.text: 算法 ：Whirlpool 散列（Whirlpool）。 512 位分组、512 位密钥与 8×8 状态 Whirlpool 的压缩函数是一个专用 512 位分组密码 W：分组 512 位、密钥 512 位、10 轮。状态写成 8×8 的 GF(2^8) 字节矩阵，每轮依次做字节代换 SB、列移位 SC、行混合 MR 与轮密钥加 AK；密钥编排复用同一组轮函数，只把轮常数换成密钥调度常数。 Miyaguchi–Preneel 与 Merkle–Damgård 消息按 512 位分组，压缩函数用 Miyaguchi–Preneel 构造： H_i = W_{H_{i-1}}(M_i) ⊕ M_i ⊕ H_{i-1} 上一链值既是分组密码的密钥，又是前馈项；消息块既是被加密的明文，又是前馈项。外层是 Merkle–Damgård 迭代，消息长度上限 2^256 位，输出 512 位摘要。 Whirlpool 采用 AES 式的宽轨迹设计：SB、SC、MR 三层在 8×8 状态上提供字节级非线性与行列扩散，10 轮足以把单字节差异摊到整个状态。512 位摘要把生日碰撞界推到 2^256，比 256 位摘要多出一截安全边际；它不依赖 64 位乘法，8 位微控制器和 64 位 CPU 都能实现，这是 NESSIE 看重它的原因。 实现取向 Whirlpool 的轮函数只有查表和异或，8 位实现可以把 8×8 状态放进寄存器；64 位实现则用 8 个 64 位字打包列，一次处理一整列。它没有 SHA-2 的 32/64 位加法链，也没有 SHA-3 的 Keccak 置换，性能曲线更接近 AES。 Whirlpool 是 NESSIE 2003 选出的散列之一，也是 ISO/IEC 10118-3 的 Dedicated Hash-Function 7；2018 年第四版仍保留它。它常被放进“SHA-2 之外的 512 位散列”清单，用于需要长摘要、又不想引入 SHA-3 新构造的旧系统。 典型落点 它能出现在数字签名、文件完整性清单和磁盘加密的口令派生链里；这些场景看中的是 512 位输出和成熟实现，而不是新设计。新协议若没有兼容约束，通常直接选 SHA-512 或 SHA-3-512。 Whirlpool 外层是 Merkle–Damgård，天然可做长度扩展：知道 H(M) 的人不需要密钥就能算出 H(M pad X)。所以它不能单独当 MAC 用，必须套 HMAC 或改用带密钥的构造。作为 512 位散列，生日碰撞界是 2^256；这不等于“后量子安全”，Grover 类搜索会把理想安全强度降到约 2^256 的平方根级别。全 10 轮尚无实用碰撞，但缩减轮区分器说明轮函数并非无懈可击。Whirlpool 不提供认证加密，也不 hiding 任何输入；它只保证压缩后的摘要难以碰撞。把摘要截短会直接降低碰撞成本，512 位输出不应被截到 256 位以下再用于抗碰撞场景。 Whirlpool 由 Paulo Barreto 与 Vincent Rijmen 设计，2000 年提交 NESSIE；2001 年的 Whirlpool-T 调整了扩散矩阵；2003 年最终版改用新的 S 盒与循环矩阵，形成现在的 10 轮版本。它在 NESSIE 2003 进入 portfolio，随后进入 ISO/IEC 10118-3，2018 年随第四版继续保留。 版本差异 Whirlpool-0 使用随机生成的 S 盒，Whirlpool-T 换用结构化 S 盒并调整 MR，最终版再换 S 盒与循环矩阵。三个版本的摘要互不兼容，旧系统升级时必须重新计算所有历史摘要。 技术参数与复算边界 该条目的形式模型是 \(h=H(M),\quad H:\{0,1\}^{ }\to\{0,1\}^{n}\)。输入：输入：Whirlpool 散列的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：M 任意长度消息，h 为 n 位摘要。 预期输出：按 Whirlpool 散列 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。 复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。 - items.title: 斯蒂芬·威斯纳
items.text: 人物 ：斯蒂芬·威斯纳（Stephen Wiesner）。斯蒂芬·威斯纳，美国物理学家，哥伦比亚大学博士，后长期任教于以色列海法大学。约 1970 年写下《共轭编码》，提出量子货币与复用信道等构想——因思想过于超前而屡遭拒稿，沉睡十余年后被贝内特与布拉萨德重新发现，成为量子密码学的源头文献。 威斯纳约 1970 年写成的《共轭编码》手稿接连被期刊拒稿，此后沉睡十余年；直到贝内特与布拉萨德把它从故纸堆里翻出来，才催生出 BB84。这篇「史上被拒稿最久的奠基论文」最终于 1983 年发表在一份计算机理论通讯上。保留这一人物条目的理由，是它能把一个具体的人与其时代、工作和相邻实体区分开；人物影响不自动等于其个人独力完成的结果。 「量子态测不准、抄不走——这本身就是最诚实的封条。（意译，编者拟）」 这句话用于标识该人物在资料中的立场或表述，不把它当成制度性结论，也不把后世引用当成原始史料。 人物条目的边界：史料有限，纪念性说法、归属争议和后世追认都要与可核生平分开。不把集体成果、同名算法或同名事件自动归到本人；不把一句名言当成其全部思想。 可核角色与证据链 斯蒂芬·威斯纳归入基础与术语，登记时代为量子转折。该条目只登记有来源支持的教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件与可核同行评价。来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 斯蒂芬·威斯纳；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews。 没有来源支持的出生、死亡、家庭、师承、奖项、论文数量和任职日期不补写；同名人物不合并；后人归功与本人文本分开。 同名概念的分界 斯蒂芬·威斯纳只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 斯蒂芬·威斯纳（Tier 3）；MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews（Tier 2）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 读法：从对象到证据 读 斯蒂芬·威斯纳 先固定对象：它是什么类型、属于基础与术语的哪一段、与哪些条目相邻。再列证据：谁在何时说了什么、locator 在哪、是否为一手材料。最后写边界：哪些结论只是模型关系，哪些仍待核。 不要把目录位置当参数表，不要把标题当定理，也不要把一次示例当普适结论；这三类是该条目明确拒绝的误读。 复核清单 检查 斯蒂芬·威斯纳 时逐项回答：对象类型是否固定；时间、地点、参与者是否各有来源；文本、器物或机构记录是否区分一手与二手；相邻条目是否被误并；没有来源的空白是否明确留空。五项中任何一项只能靠猜测，就停在“待核”，不把叙事写成证明。 - Wikipedia search entry for 斯蒂芬·威斯纳. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E6%96%AF%E8%92%82%E8%8A%AC%C2%B7%E5%A8%81%E6%96%AF%E7%BA%B3 - MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive, University of St Andrews. https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/ 角色关系模型 只登记四类关系：教育/任职机构、公开文本或专利、参与的标准/机器/事件、可核同行评价。每条关系都要有来源；没有来源的师承、奖项和私生活不进入模型。

items.title: XSalsa20 流密码
items.text: 算法 ：XSalsa20 流密码（XSalsa20）。 Salsa20 的 512 位状态 Salsa20 把 256 位密钥、64 位 nonce、64 位块计数器和 128 位常量排成 16 个 32 位字的 4×4 矩阵。20 轮 ARX（32 位加、旋转、异或）后，把结果加回输入，得到 64 字节密钥流块。它没有 S 盒，也没有秘密下标查表。 XSalsa20 先派生子密钥 XSalsa20 把 nonce 扩到 192 位：先用密钥和前 128 位 nonce 跑 HSalsa20。HSalsa20 与 Salsa20 共用 20 轮核心，但省略最后的输入加法，取 8 个特定字组成 256 位子密钥；再用该子密钥、剩余 64 位 nonce 和 64 位块计数器运行标准 Salsa20/20 生成密钥流。 长 nonce 的意义 64 位 nonce 在同一密钥下随机生成时，约 2^32 条消息就会出现生日碰撞；192 位 nonce 把碰撞风险推到约 2^96 条消息。对“每条消息随机 nonce”的协议，这比维护全局计数器更简单。 XSalsa20 的动机是 nonce 管理，而不是新的轮函数。NaCl 的 crypto_box 用 X25519 协商密钥、XSalsa20 加密、Poly1305 认证；每条消息可以独立随机 192 位 nonce，不需要跨会话共享计数器。它保持 Salsa20 的速度和 ARX 的侧信道特性，只增加一次 HSalsa20 子密钥派生，成本小于一个 Salsa20 输出块。SKEW 2011 的论文证明：对 XSalsa20 的快速攻击可以转化为对 Salsa20 的攻击，因此它的安全性归约到 Salsa20。 libsodium 把 XSalsa20/20 暴露为 crypto_stream 和 crypto_stream_xor；NaCl 的 crypto_box 组合 XSalsa20 与 Poly1305；许多语言绑定和消息加密库沿用这一组合。它适合需要长 nonce、随机 nonce、软件高速的协议。它不是 TLS 标准套件；TLS 1.3 采用 ChaCha20-Poly1305 或 AES-GCM，XSalsa20 更多出现在 NaCl 生态和自定义协议中。 XSalsa20 只提供机密性，不提供完整性；必须配 Poly1305 或上层 AEAD。nonce 仍然必须唯一：同一 key/nonce 重用会让两条密钥流相同，密文异或即明文异或。192 位 nonce 只是把碰撞概率降到可接受水平，不是允许重复使用。64 位块计数器给单对 key/nonce 约 2^64 个 64 字节块的上限；超过后计数器回绕，必须换 key 或 nonce。ARX 软件实现天然抵抗计时攻击，但硬件功耗/电磁分析仍可能恢复状态；HSalsa20 也不是通用 KDF，不应把同一密钥跨用途复用。 Salsa20 由 Bernstein 在 2005 年设计，Salsa20/12 进入 eSTREAM 软件 portfolio。2008 年 Bernstein 提出 XSalsa20，把 nonce 扩到 192 位并给出安全归约；NaCl 随后把 XSalsa20+Poly1305 用于 crypto_box，libsodium 延续这一组合。它是 ARX 流密码和“随机 nonce”设计的重要节点。 技术参数与复算边界 该条目的形式模型是 \(C=E_K(P;r),\qquad P=D_K(C)\)。输入：输入：XSalsa20 流密码的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：P 明文，C 密文，K 密钥，r 随机化参数。 预期输出：按 XSalsa20 流密码 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。 复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。 参数与状态规模 公式 \(C=E_K(P;r),\qquad P=D_K(C)\) 的输入、输出和单位必须逐项登记；复算顺序为：1. 按算法规范编码输入 2. 在密钥控制下执行轮函数 3. 输出密文并检查长度与格式。 状态规模、密钥长度、分组长度和轮数决定复杂度；这些量不能从标题推断，必须以标准或实现文档为准。 - items.title: 黄道杀手 340 密文
items.text: 器物 ：黄道杀手 340 密文（Zodiac 340 Cipher）。 实物/文献 ：黄道杀手 340 密文（Zodiac 340 Cipher）。1969 年 11 月 8 日黄道杀手寄给《旧金山纪事报》的 340 字符密文，51 年间令 FBI 与全球爱好者束手无策；2020 年 12 月，三人民间团队以交叉比对法破译，读出「我希望你们在抓捕我时玩得开心」等语句，成为近年最轰动的民间密码破解。档案坐标：密件册 · 1969 年 11 月 · 美国旧金山 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： detective 。该条目只陈述项目档案中可核的实物或文献信息，不把展签、网络转述或复制品当成原件。 这份材料值得保留，是因为它把抽象的密码学问题落到一个可观察的对象上：破解文本全文大意：「我希望你们在抓捕我时玩得开心。我不怕毒气室，因为它会把我更快送上天，因为我现在已经有足够多的奴隶为我劳作……」，句中提及「天堂」与「奴隶」，呼应杀手自比极乐主宰的幻想；其余段落仍含拼写错误与自创词，学界对破解结论仍有保留意见。它的价值在于提供问题入口，而不是替所有相关谜题给出答案。 阅读这件器物时，抓住三个问题：谁持有或操作它、它把什么结构约束变成可验证的步骤、失败时留下什么可见证据。实物参数只写馆藏、铭文或档案能支持的数值。 该器物本身不构成安全系统；原件、复制品与复原模型混用，铭文误读，或缺少馆藏记录时，不能据此推断年代、作者或用途。 密件册 · 1969 年 11 月 · 美国旧金山 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： detective 。1969 年 11 月 8 日黄道杀手寄给《旧金山纪事报》的 340 字符密文，51 年间令 FBI 与全球爱好者束手无策；2020 年 12 月，三人民间团队以交叉比对法破译，读出「我希望你们在抓捕我时玩得开心」等语句，成为近年最轰动的民间密码破解。 物证模型与不确定性 黄道杀手 340 密文按输入（尺寸、材质、铭文、结构或操作记录）—结构（可见部件与连接关系）—操作（同时代的使用方式）—证据（馆藏、档案、铭文或技术手册）阅读。来源链包括：Wikipedia search entry for 黄道杀手 340 密文；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights；Museum/collection record for 黄道杀手 340 密文。 原件、复制品、复原模型和照片必须分开；年代、作者、用途、铭文读法有争议时并列保留；没有馆藏或档案支持的参数不写成确定值。 同名概念的分界 黄道杀手 340 密文只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 黄道杀手 340 密文（Tier 3）；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights（Tier 1）；Museum/collection record for 黄道杀手 340 密文（Tier 1）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 读法：从对象到证据 读 黄道杀手 340 密文 先固定对象：它是什么类型、属于应用安全工程的哪一段、与哪些条目相邻。再列证据：谁在何时说了什么、locator 在哪、是否为一手材料。最后写边界：哪些结论只是模型关系，哪些仍待核。 不要把目录位置当参数表，不要把标题当定理，也不要把一次示例当普适结论；这三类是该条目明确拒绝的误读。 - items.title: 齐默尔曼电报
items.text: 器物 ：齐默尔曼电报（The Zimmermann Telegram）。 实物/文献 ：齐默尔曼电报（The Zimmermann Telegram）。齐默尔曼电报：1917 年 1 月德国外长密令墨西哥进攻美国的电文。伦敦海军部 40 号房破译它之后，美国加入了第一次世界大战。档案坐标：密件册 · 1917 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： adfgvx 。该条目只陈述项目档案中可核的实物或文献信息，不把展签、网络转述或复制品当成原件。 这份材料值得保留，是因为它把抽象的密码学问题落到一个可观察的对象上：—— 齐默尔曼电报（1917 年 1 月 16 日，德译英节选） 「我们打算于二月一日起开始无限制潜艇战。尽管如此，我们将设法使美利坚合众国保持中立。倘若此事不能成功，我们提议与墨西哥结盟，基础如下：共同作战、共同媾和、慷慨的财政支持，以及我方谅解墨西哥将收复其在得克萨斯、新墨西哥与亚利桑那的失地。细节由你酌定。一旦与美国开战确凿无疑，请即刻将上述内容极其秘密地知会贵国总统，并建议他主动邀请日本立即加入，同时由我们在日墨之间斡旋。」 🤔 反事实思考：如果这份电报晚发一个月——美国已经因潜艇袭击而愤怒参战——它就只是一份普通的外交文件，而非改变战争走向的关键。历史的转折，往往取决于时机与破译的巧合。它的价值在于提供问题入口，而不是替所有相关谜题给出答案。 阅读这件器物时，抓住三个问题：谁持有或操作它、它把什么结构约束变成可验证的步骤、失败时留下什么可见证据。实物参数只写馆藏、铭文或档案能支持的数值。 该器物本身不构成安全系统；原件、复制品与复原模型混用，铭文误读，或缺少馆藏记录时，不能据此推断年代、作者或用途。 密件册 · 1917 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： adfgvx 。齐默尔曼电报：1917 年 1 月德国外长密令墨西哥进攻美国的电文。 物证模型与不确定性 齐默尔曼电报按输入（尺寸、材质、铭文、结构或操作记录）—结构（可见部件与连接关系）—操作（同时代的使用方式）—证据（馆藏、档案、铭文或技术手册）阅读。来源链包括：Wikipedia search entry for 齐默尔曼电报；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights；Museum/collection record for 齐默尔曼电报。 原件、复制品、复原模型和照片必须分开；年代、作者、用途、铭文读法有争议时并列保留；没有馆藏或档案支持的参数不写成确定值。 同名概念的分界 齐默尔曼电报只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 齐默尔曼电报（Tier 3）；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights（Tier 1）；Museum/collection record for 齐默尔曼电报（Tier 1）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 读法：从对象到证据 读 齐默尔曼电报 先固定对象：它是什么类型、属于应用安全工程的哪一段、与哪些条目相邻。再列证据：谁在何时说了什么、locator 在哪、是否为一手材料。最后写边界：哪些结论只是模型关系，哪些仍待核。 不要把目录位置当参数表，不要把标题当定理，也不要把一次示例当普适结论；这三类是该条目明确拒绝的误读。 复核清单 检查 齐默尔曼电报 时逐项回答：对象类型是否固定；时间、地点、参与者是否各有来源；文本、器物或机构记录是否区分一手与二手；相邻条目是否被误并；没有来源的空白是否明确留空。五项中任何一项只能靠猜测，就停在“待核”，不把叙事写成证明。 - items.text: 器物 ：黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文（The Zodiac "My Name Is" 13-Character Cipher）。 实物/文献 ：黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文（The Zodiac "My Name Is" 13-Character Cipher）。1969 年 11 月，自称「黄道十二宫」的连环杀手向《旧金山纪事报》寄出密文，宣称其中 13 个字符暗藏他的真实姓名。五十年间无数人尝试破解，至今未获公认答案，成为悬案中最著名的未解密码之一。档案坐标：密件册 · 1969 年 · 美国旧金山湾区 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： detective 。该条目只陈述项目档案中可核的实物或文献信息，不把展签、网络转述或复制品当成原件。 这份材料值得保留，是因为它把抽象的密码学问题落到一个可观察的对象上：这封「我的名字是」信件中，13 个字符据称代表凶手的真名。业余与专业密码学家提出过数百种解法，从斯拉夫姓氏到精巧的拼图，但没有任何一种得到官方与公众的一致认可。即使 FBI 在 2020 年宣布破解 340 字符的 z340 密文时，也明确表示这 13 字符仍未解开，令其成为密码史上最令人着迷的悬案之一。它的价值在于提供问题入口，而不是替所有相关谜题给出答案。 阅读这件器物时，抓住三个问题：谁持有或操作它、它把什么结构约束变成可验证的步骤、失败时留下什么可见证据。实物参数只写馆藏、铭文或档案能支持的数值。 该器物本身不构成安全系统；原件、复制品与复原模型混用，铭文误读，或缺少馆藏记录时，不能据此推断年代、作者或用途。 密件册 · 1969 年 · 美国旧金山湾区 · 性质：真实史料 / Real record · 关联游戏： detective 。1969 年 11 月，自称「黄道十二宫」的连环杀手向《旧金山纪事报》寄出密文，宣称其中 13 个字符暗藏他的真实姓名。 物证模型与不确定性 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文按输入（尺寸、材质、铭文、结构或操作记录）—结构（可见部件与连接关系）—操作（同时代的使用方式）—证据（馆藏、档案、铭文或技术手册）阅读。来源链包括：Wikipedia search entry for 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights；Museum/collection record for 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文。 原件、复制品、复原模型和照片必须分开；年代、作者、用途、铭文读法有争议时并列保留；没有馆藏或档案支持的参数不写成确定值。 同名概念的分界 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文只对自身登记对象负责。与相邻条目的名称可能重叠，该条目不把别条的事实并入，也不用一个版本来覆盖另一个版本。 遇到同名对象时先查三项：类型（人物/事件/器物/术语）、时间、来源机构；三项不能同时对上，就当作不同条目处理。 来源等级与未核项 该条目来源账本包括：Wikipedia search entry for 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文（Tier 3）；National Museum of China, Collection Highlights（Tier 1）；Museum/collection record for 黄道十二宫杀手「我的名字是」13 字符密文（Tier 1）。 Tier 1/2 只说明来源类型，不等于每条断言都逐页核过；正文中没有来源支持的日期、数量、角色和参数保持空白。二手概述与一手材料冲突时，以一手材料为准；争议不静默覆盖，保留在边界节。 - items.title: 齐加尔斯基记录表
items.text: 术语 ：齐加尔斯基记录表（Zygalski Sheet）。 female 与指示 在 1940 年 5 月之前，Enigma 操作员把三字母消息密钥加密两次，形成六字母指示。若消息密钥的同一字母在两次加密后得到相同密文字母，就得到 1-4、2-5 或 3-6 位的 female。并非所有转子位置都能产生 female；这给出一组可筛选的约束。 穿孔表 固定转子顺序与左转子位置（26 种），对其余两个转子的 26×26 个位置逐一计算：若某位置可能产生 female，就在对应格子打孔。3 转子时期有 6 种顺序，因此每套 6×26=156 张表；每张表是 26×26 网格，约 1,000 个孔。多张表按指示字母平移叠加，孔位相交；约 10-12 条 female 后只剩一个透光孔，即候选设置。5 转子时期有 60 种顺序，需 1,560 张表。 Zygalski 表把“可能性”变成可叠加的二维集合：每张表不是一条猜测，而是一个完整的位置约束。它展示了用组合筛选替代逐条试解的思路，也说明为什么波兰与英国必须为每一种转子顺序预制表。与 Bombe 不同，Zygalski 表不依赖 crib，也不要求已知明文；它只利用双倍加密指示的结构。它也不是“穷举所有 26^3 位置”：表把位置空间压缩成孔位交集，但制表与平移仍需大量人工。 1.确认指示使用双倍加密，且报文日期在同一密钥期。2.收集 female，记录其 1-4、2-5 或 3-6 类型。3.对每个转子顺序与左转子位置取对应表。4.按指示字母平移表，叠加并观察透光孔。5.把唯一孔位转成中/右转子位置，回到 Enigma 验证。 不能怎么用 不能用于 1940 年 5 月后的单次加密指示；不能把一张表当一个完整密钥；不能忽略转子顺序变化与五转子时期的 1,560 张规模。 1.指示程序改变：单次加密后不再产生 female，整套方法失效。2.数据不足：female 太少时孔位交集不唯一。3.表的制造误差：错孔或漏孔会直接排除正确设置。4.转子顺序或左转子位置不在预制范围内：必须另制表。5.把透光孔当最终明文：它只给出候选设置，仍需机器验证与解密。 Henryk Zygalski 在 1938 年秋提出穿孔表方法。1938 年 12 月德国增加到 5 个转子，转子顺序从 6 种增至 60 种，所需表从 156 张增至 1,560 张，波兰无法独立完成。英国 Bletchley Park 在 John Jeffreys 组织下制表并送到波兰，1940 年 1 月 17 日 Enigma 再次被读取。 - Wikipedia search entry for 齐加尔斯基记录表. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E9%BD%90%E5%8A%A0%E5%B0%94%E6%96%AF%E5%9F%BA%E8%AE%B0%E5%BD%95%E8%A1%A8 - RFC 4949: Internet Security Glossary, Version 2. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4949 定义检查模型 上位概念 → 区别特征 → 正例 → 反例 → 易混边界。正例必须落在外延内；反例必须刚好跨过边界；同义词不能代替定义。

items.title: Caesar cipher
items.text: A Caesar cipher rotates an alphabet by one fixed offset. This lesson explicitly uses modern A–Z: A=0, …, Z=25 and k in 0…25. Encryption is c=(m+k) mod 26; decryption is m=(c−k) mod 26. Repeated plaintext letters retain a single substitution. With k=3, A→D, X→A and HELLO→KHOOR. Modulo here returns a value in 0…25, including when decryption first produces a negative number. Handling spaces, case and punctuation requires a separate implementation convention. It separates plaintext, ciphertext, algorithm and key. Changing k changes the transformation while leaving the rule public. A complete hand calculation shows why reversibility and secrecy are different properties: being able to undo a transformation says nothing about whether an attacker can cheaply try every key. Use it for lessons and letter puzzles, not real confidentiality. Specify the alphabet and direction, transform the letters, then verify by reversing the operation. The 26-letter classroom convention is not a reconstruction of an ancient Roman alphabet or message format. There are 26 shifts including the identity k=0, or 25 nonidentity shifts. Exhaustion produces a list containing the original. A very short message may leave several plausible readings, so trying every key does not guarantee a unique interpretation. Longer natural-language messages also retain repetition and frequency clues. The name is associated with Julius Caesar. Suetonius, Life of Julius Caesar §56, describes altered letters in confidential correspondence and mentions D in place of A. This is an ancient written account, not evidence that Caesar invented substitution ciphers; the modular formula above is a modern teaching formulation. - Chris Savarese and Brian Hart, The Caesar Cipher, Trinity College - Suetonius, The Life of Julius Caesar, §56.6, J. C. Rolfe translation; Lexundria transcription - A. Menezes, P. van Oorschot and S. Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography, CRC Press, 1996, Chapter 7 - Duke University, Math Everywhere, Cryptography — Course Notes

items.title: Frequency analysis
items.text: Count symbols, then test mapping hypotheses against language structure. A fixed monoalphabetic substitution relabels counts: for substitution π, countC(y)=countM(π⁻¹(y)). Choose counting units and preprocessing, inspect single symbols, repeats and combinations, propose mappings, then test them across the whole text. Reference frequencies guide hypotheses; they are not a literal decoding table. A large keyspace need not hide structure. Even with many possible substitution tables, redundancy can rule out large classes of guesses. It is also an introduction to statistical inference: collect evidence, form a hypothesis and test it rather than treating the tallest bar as an answer. Apply it to classroom substitution and shift ciphers. Follow single-letter counts with pairs, repeated letters, word lengths and context. A periodic polyalphabetic cipher may permit separate analysis of position classes after a candidate period is chosen. Transposition preserves total letter counts, but counts alone do not reconstruct the order. It fails when evidence does not fit the model: too little text, unusual subject matter, the wrong language or a changing substitution. Common English frequency patterns do not make E the leader in every short message. In our counterexample BANANA, A occurs three times, N twice and B once. After shifting to EDQDQD, D leads and represents A, not E. Classical cryptanalysis and cipher design developed around visible structure: fixed substitution preserves counts, while changing alphabets disrupts that simple correspondence. This account does not assign an invention date without examining the historical record. HAC Chapter 7 provides a comparison of transposition, monoalphabetic, polyalphabetic and rotor methods. - A. Menezes, P. van Oorschot and S. Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography, CRC Press, 1996, Chapter 7 - Duke University, Math Everywhere, Cryptography — Course Notes - Paul Krzyzanowski, Rutgers University, CS 419, Part 1 — Foundations and Classical Ciphers

items.title: Enigma
items.text: Enigma is a family of electromechanical machines. In a typical reflecting design, current passes through rotors, is paired by a reflector and returns through the rotors to a lamp; some models add a plugboard. Stepping changes the mapping, so repeated presses can produce different letters. Wiring and stepping are model-specific. At a frozen state, let F map inputs toward the reflector and U pair reflector contacts. Then E=F⁻¹∘U∘F. If U²=I and U has no fixed points, E²=I and E(x)≠x. This explains the structure, not a complete emulator. It turns a fixed alphabet into a changing state machine and makes system-level questions concrete. Hardware still depends on settings, message procedures and coordinated operation. Understanding a circuit is a starting point, not a proof of security. Use this entry for history, mechanism studies and permutation exercises. For a real model, distinguish rotor order, ring settings, starting positions, plugboard and stepping rules. Decryption must recreate the required initial state and procedure rather than reuse the rotors where encryption ended. A typical reflecting Enigma never maps a letter to itself, ruling out some plaintext guesses. Stepping regularities, message procedures and operator habits can add exploitable conditions. Models and communication periods pose different tasks. Neither one large keyspace number nor one historical success describes all Enigma traffic. The US National Cryptologic Museum describes Polish mathematical work on Enigma in 1932 and names Rejewski, Zygalski and Różycki. That institutional account supports this limited historical summary; it does not justify crediting all results to one person. Models, procedures and phases of cryptanalysis need separate accounts. - Crypto Museum, Enigma cipher machines - Crypto Museum, Enigma — How it works - NSA/CSS National Cryptologic Museum, New Polish Enigma Exhibit, 11 December 2007

items.title: AES: Advanced Encryption Standard
items.text: AES is a symmetric block cipher: for a fixed key it reversibly maps 128-bit blocks to 128-bit blocks. AES-128/192/256 use different key lengths, the same block length and 10/12/14 rounds. The state contains 16 bytes. After initial AddRoundKey, ordinary rounds apply SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns and AddRoundKey; the final round omits MixColumns. Key expansion supplies round keys. Nonlinear substitution and diffusion work together; no single operation explains the whole security argument. It is a standardized building block with precisely testable outputs. Separate correctness of the block transformation, the mode handling messages, and system management of keys and authentication. Matching one standard vector checks that input/output pair; it does not prove side-channel resistance or application security. TLS 1.3 is one specific use. RFC 9846, which obsoletes RFC 8446, lists AES-GCM and AES-CCM suites alongside ChaCha20-Poly1305. AES is therefore not the only modern choice, and AES-ECB is not a TLS 1.3 AEAD suite. A block primitive and a protocol construction are different layers. A fixed-key block transformation is deterministic; direct independent use on messages reveals repeated-block structure. GCM adds confidentiality and authentication but requires correct IV uniqueness under a key; reuse undermines its assurances. A birthday collision bound is not an AES key length. The ECB single-block example below is only a transformation test, not a recommendation to protect messages with ECB. NIST began the AES process in 1997 and announced Rijndael’s selection on October 2, 2000. FIPS 197 was published in 2001. Its 2023 update improved presentation without changing the algorithm. Initiation, selection, publication and effective dates are separate events. - NIST, FIPS 197-upd1, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), 2023 - NIST, AES Development archive - NIST CSRC, FIPS 197 publication page - Morris Dworkin, NIST SP 800-38A, Recommendation for Block Cipher Modes of Operation, 2001 - Morris Dworkin, NIST SP 800-38D, GCM and GMAC, 2007 - Eric Rescorla, RFC 9846, The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3; obsoletes RFC 8446 Single-block check only: key 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c, input 6bc1bee22e409f96e93d7e117393172a, output 3ad77bb40d7a3660a89ecaf32466ef97. Source: NIST SP 800-38A Appendix F.1.1, first block. verify.mjs recomputes it using Node/OpenSSL and checks inversion. These public test values are not operational keys.

items.title: RSA
items.text: RSA uses related public and private keys. In the two-prime teaching case, n=pq, λ(n)=lcm(p−1,q−1), gcd(e,λ(n))=1 and ed≡1 mod λ(n). The public key includes n and e; secret values such as d require protection. For an in-range integer representative m, the primitives compute c=mᵉ mod n and m=cᵈ mod n. Small numbers explain algebra, not a complete encryption or signature scheme. It separates public operations from private capabilities. A signer can also produce verifiable evidence without revealing the signing secret. Public-key techniques do not remove trust questions: a user still needs to establish whose key is being used and what identity the message is bound to. RFC 8017 separately defines RSAES encryption and RSASSA signature schemes, including RSAES-OAEP and RSASSA-PSS. Signing is not simply encrypting with the private key TLS 1.3 as specified by RFC 9846 illustrates the distinction: RSA signatures may authenticate peers, while legacy RSA key transport is absent. Bare exponentiation is deterministic and algebraically structured, so it cannot directly secure arbitrary messages. Factoring n enables recovery of the relevant secret arithmetic, but difficulty of factoring is not a complete security proof for every RSA construction. Encoding, validation and key exposure matter alongside the algebra. Rivest, Shamir and Adleman published A Method for Obtaining Digital Signatures and Public-Key Cryptosystems in 1978. RFC 8017 republished PKCS 1 v2.2 in 2016. The paper and specification show different layers: a mathematical construction and carefully defined schemes, encodings and interchange rules. - R. L. Rivest, A. Shamir and L. Adleman, A Method for Obtaining Digital Signatures and Public-Key Cryptosystems, Communications of the ACM 21(2), 1978, pp. 120–126 - K. Moriarty et al., RFC 8017, PKCS 1: RSA Cryptography Specifications Version 2.2, November 2016 - Eric Rescorla, RFC 9846, The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3; obsoletes RFC 8446 Public teaching parameters: p=61, q=53, n=3233 and λ(n)=780. Choose e=17 and d=413: 17×413=7021≡1 mod 780. For m=65, c=2790 and 2790^413 mod 3233=65. verify.mjs checks every representative 0…3232. These tiny public numbers provide no real secrecy.

items.title: Post-quantum cryptography
items.text: Post-quantum cryptography targets classical and quantum adversaries while running on conventional computers. The name describes the threat model, not a requirement for quantum hardware or quantum communication. Separate tasks: a KEM establishes a shared secret; a signature scheme signs and verifies. ML-KEM relates to Module Learning with Errors, while SLH-DSA is a stateless hash-based signature scheme. These are distinct constructions, not one universal quantum encryption algorithm. Migration concerns long-lived data and systems. This entry does not predict when a machine could attack operational keys. Separating constructions, parameters and protocols helps distinguish a design goal and a believed hard problem from an unconditional security proof. NIST FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM for establishing a shared secret over a public channel, after which suitable symmetric constructions perform subsequent tasks. FIPS 204 specifies ML-DSA and FIPS 205 SLH-DSA for signatures, not the same encapsulation task. Integration still needs protocol authentication, key management and formats. Standardization is not a permanent security guarantee. FIPS 203/204 describe believed resistance, not proof that every attack fails. Parameters, implementations and protocols still need analysis. Their publication pages include errata or potential-update notes, which maintainers must read alongside the standards. This conceptual entry does not implement homemade ML-KEM or present tiny lattice arithmetic as its validation. Standard-specific vectors and parameter checks belong in separate algorithm entries. NIST published FIPS 203, 204 and 205 on August 13, 2024, covering ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA respectively. This records three identified final publications, not all PQC research. Candidates, drafts and final standards must remain distinct. Status statements reflect pages consulted on October 24, 2026. - NIST CSRC, Post-Quantum Cryptography project - NIST, What Is Post-Quantum Cryptography? - NIST, FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, August 13, 2024 - NIST, FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard, August 13, 2024 - NIST, FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard, August 13, 2024 - NSA/CSS, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and Quantum Cryptography (QC)

items.title: 3DES/TDEA: extending an old cipher with three DES passes
items.text: Algorithm : Triple DES (3DES 三重数据加密). TDEA is not a new block cipher; it uses DES three times as a "cryptographic engine". It keeps the 64-bit DES block and applies encrypt-decrypt-encrypt with a key bundle of three DES keys: C = E_K3(D_K2(E_K1(P))) Encryption first encrypts with K1, decrypts with K2, and encrypts with K3. Decryption uses the same keys in reverse order: P = D_K1(E_K2(D_K3(C))) The middle decryption step is not a mistake: the EDE structure makes the three-key option collapse to single DES when K1=K2=K3, which helps compatibility with legacy systems. TDEA keeps a 64-bit block and performs 3×16=48 DES rounds internally; it expands key material, not the block. TDEA has three historical keying options: 1-key (K1=K2=K3), 2-key (K1=K3) and 3-key (three independent keys). These names describe the number of independent keys in the bundle; FIPS 46-3 numbers its Keying Options differently (Option 1 is three independent keys, Option 3 is three identical keys). Counting parity bits, their nominal lengths are 64, 128 and 192 bits; the effective bits used by the algorithm are 56, 112 and 168. Current SP 800-67 Revision 2 permits only 3-key for encryption, prohibits 2-key for cryptographic protection, and treats 1-key as a historical option equivalent to single DES. Nominal bits are not security strength: NIST assigns about 80 bits of security to 2-key TDEA and about 112 bits to 3-key TDEA. TDEA was the transition from DES to AES. It reused deployed DES hardware and code and increased key material without replacing the block engine, so 1990s systems could extend their service life quickly. FIPS 46-3 recognized TDEA as a federal algorithm in 1999 while demoting single DES to legacy systems only. It is also a warning about nominal key length. A 3-key TDEA bundle has 192 nominal key bits and 168 effective bits, but public security assessment gives it about 112 bits; 2-key TDEA is nominally 128 bits with 112 effective bits but about 80 bits in strength. Treating 192 or 168 as the security level overstates the margin. TDEA's 64-bit block also creates birthday collisions, making high-volume protocols weaker than the key length suggests. TDEA's historical role was not long-term adequacy but adequacy during a migration window. Once AES was available and migration was affordable, staying on TDEA became a compatibility choice rather than a security choice. Typical TDEA deployments were legacy systems in federal agencies and older network protocols. It appeared where DES hardware had to be reused: government terminals, old devices and early TLS/VPN configurations. FIPS 46-3 explicitly restricted single DES to legacy systems and treated TDEA as the federal symmetric encryption choice of that time; that reflects the 1999 transition policy, not today's approval status. TDEA is normally used with a mode of operation. ECB encrypts each 64-bit block independently; CBC needs an initialization vector and hides repetition; CFB/OFB turn the block cipher into a stream-like generator. A mode does not change the 64-bit block or the 48-round engine, and cannot repair key options or data-volume limits. Concrete modes belong to the modes entity and are not detailed here. In modern protocols TDEA mainly survives as a compatibility option. As long as a protocol still allows it, long connections and high data volumes expose the 64-bit birthday bound; the ability to still decrypt old data and the duty to encrypt new data are different questions. Two-key TDEA encryption was disallowed after 2015; three-key TDEA encryption was disallowed after December 31, 2023. NIST announced the withdrawal of SP 800-67 Revision 2 in 2023 and formally withdrew it on January 1, 2024. After withdrawal, TDEA is allowed only for decryption, key unwrapping and MAC verification of already-protected data, not for new encryption protection. These dates are policy status, not a physical moment when the algorithm suddenly stopped working. They mean new systems should not choose TDEA, while old systems need risk-based migration and continued ability to decrypt legacy data. NIST SP 800-57 assigns about 80 bits of security strength to 2-key TDEA and about 112 bits to 3-key TDEA. A 3-key bundle has 192 nominal key bits and 168 effective bits but only 112 bits of assessed strength; this is an assessment result, not an implementation defect. Both 80 and 112 bits are below a modern 128-bit target and cannot protect long-term new data. TDEA still has a 64-bit block. SP 800-67 Revision 2 limits encryption under a single 3-key bundle to 2²⁰ 64-bit blocks (8 MiB) and explicitly prohibits using 2-key TDEA for cryptographic protection. That standard limit is much stricter than the birthday bound. The birthday bound itself makes collisions non-negligible after about 2³² blocks (about 32 GiB); Sweet32-style attacks use repeated ciphertext blocks in long connections to recover parts of plaintext. TDEA's 168 effective key bits and 112-bit security strength cannot compensate for a 64-bit block: the birthday bound is set by block size, not key size. TDEA security depends on the quality of all three DES keys. SP 800-67 requires avoiding DES weak and semi-weak keys and explicitly prohibits three identical keys. If all three keys are the same DES weak key, TDEA degenerates to single DES under that weak key: encrypting twice with the same weak key returns the plaintext (E_K(E_K(P))=P); using three identical keys and calling it 3DES is only an expensive wrapper around single DES. The 1-key option (K1=K2=K3) is mathematically single DES. It appears as a historical keying option in the FIPS 46-3/ANSI X9.52 context, but SP 800-67 §3.1 prohibits three identical keys, so it is not a valid TDEA key bundle either. Any deployment that treats 1-key TDEA as three-key TDEA gets only the single-DES effective key bits (56). The teaching implementation verifies only the EDE structure and known answers; it does not handle padding, modes, key management, side channels or protocol integration. Real systems also need key-bundle generation, weak-key checks, initialization vectors, data-volume limits and migration policy; these failure modes are outside the algorithm formula. TDEA standardization is connected to ANSI X9.52. FIPS 46-3 recognized TDEA as a federal algorithm in 1999 and stated that single DES was permitted only for legacy systems. NIST SP 800-67 then gave detailed TDEA recommendations; the final Revision 2 was published in 2017 and withdrawn on January 1, 2024. The transition schedule tightened step by step: two-key TDEA encryption was disallowed after 2015; three-key TDEA encryption after the end of 2023; NIST announced the withdrawal of SP 800-67 Revision 2 in 2023 and formally withdrew it in 2024. AES became the replacement, but the large installed base kept TDEA alive for two decades. This history shows that algorithm standardization is not a single event: recognition, deprecation, prohibition of new uses, withdrawal and legacy decryption support are different stages. Reading a past federal standard as present approval for new use gives the opposite conclusion. - Wikipedia search entry for 3DES 三重数据加密. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=3DES%20%E4%B8%89%E9%87%8D%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%8A%A0%E5%AF%86 - Handbook of Applied Cryptography (Menezes, van Oorschot, Vanstone). https://www.cacr.math.uwaterloo.ca/hac/ Worked example Take one published or standard test vector, record the input, the ordered steps and the byte-exact output, then compare with an independent implementation. items.title: AES: from a byte to the complete block transformation
items.text: Algorithm : Advanced Encryption Standard (AES 高级加密标准). What this algorithm does AES is a secret-key-selected reversible transformation of 128-bit blocks. This article covers the algorithm entity algorithm--aes . FIPS 197 is the related specification, not the same catalog entity. AES is not a file format, password derivation method or complete communication protocol. Variant Key bytes Nk (32-bit words) Nr (rounds) Round-key groups Expanded words --- --- --- --- --- --- AES-128 16 4 10 11 44 AES-192 24 6 12 13 52 AES-256 32 8 14 15 60 All use 16-byte blocks. The suffix describes the key, so AES-256 does not transform 256 plaintext bits at a time. FIPS 197-upd1 defines the parameters and operations; the calculations and explanatory implementation here are educational work for this article. Put the bytes in the right places For input b[0]…b[15], use s[r,c]=b[r+4c]: fill one column before the next. The input 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f is laid out as: text c0 c1 c2 c3 row0 00 04 08 0c row1 01 05 09 0d row2 02 06 0a 0e row3 03 07 0b 0f Extract output in the same column order. Each two-digit hex value is one byte. Concatenating the displayed rows is a different serialization. Rows and columns are algorithm indices, not something selected automatically by a machine’s integer endianness. Byte arithmetic is not integer arithmetic A byte represents an element of GF(2⁸). Its bits b7…b0 represent b7·x⁷+…+b1·x+b0. Coefficients are binary, so addition and subtraction are XOR. For example, 57 XOR 83=d4 ; this is not integer addition followed by a remainder. Multiply without carries, then reduce modulo m(x)=x⁸+x⁴+x³+x+1, whose bit pattern is 0x11b . Multiplication by x is called xtime: shift left and, when the old high bit was set, cancel the x⁸ term. One expression is ((a<<1) XOR ((a&0x80)?0x11b:0)) & 0xff . A version that already truncates to a byte uses 0x1b . The truncation point explains the two constants. Work through 57×02=ae , ae×02=47 , then 8e , then 07 . Since 13=10 XOR 02 XOR 01 , 57×13=07 XOR ae XOR 57=fe . All these numbers are hexadecimal. The verifier compares every one of the 65,536 byte products with a separate carryless-product/long-division calculation. SubBytes: inversion followed by an affine map For nonzero a, find z=a⁻¹ in the field. For a=0, define the intermediate z=0; zero has not acquired a multiplicative inverse. If bit i=0 is the least significant bit, the output bits are: S(a)i = zi XOR z(i+4) XOR z(i+5) XOR z(i+6) XOR z(i+7) XOR (0x63)i Indices in parentheses are modulo 8. Equivalently, S(a)=z XOR ROTL8(z,1) XOR ROTL8(z,2) XOR ROTL8(z,3) XOR ROTL8(z,4) XOR 0x63 . Thus S(00)=63; the inverse of 53 is ca and S(53)=ed. Computing a 256-entry table is possible, but table-based execution is not automatically timing-safe. Apply S independently to every state byte. The inverse S-box reverses the mapping; it is not the forward S-box applied again. Field inversion introduces nonlinearity, and the affine map is invertible. Invertibility permits decryption; it does not prove the whole cipher secure. ShiftRows connects columns Rotate row r left by r positions, for r=0,1,2,3: s'[r,c]=s[r,(c+r) mod 4] . The counting-byte state above becomes 00050a0f04090e03080d02070c01060b when serialized by columns. Values are moved rather than changed. Inversion rotates right by the same amounts. MixColumns combines four bytes Multiply each column by this matrix. Products use the field multiplication above and sums use XOR: text [02 03 01 01] [a0] [01 02 03 01] [a1] [01 01 02 03] [a2] [03 01 01 02] [a3] In round one of our example, the first column after ShiftRows is 09 28 7f 47 . Its first output is 02·09 XOR 03·28 XOR 7f XOR 47 = 12 XOR 78 XOR 7f XOR 47 = 52 ; the complete column becomes 52 9f 16 c2 . Mixing acts within one column. Alternating it with ShiftRows mixes contributions from different columns across rounds. The inverse matrix has rows 0e 0b 0d 09 , 09 0e 0b 0d , 0d 09 0e 0b , 0b 0d 09 0e . The verifier checks forward/inverse composition on 128 single-bit basis states as well as the official intermediate values. AddRoundKey introduces secret parameters A round key always contains 16 bytes. XOR them into the state using the same ordering. Repeating the operation with the same key undoes it: x XOR k XOR k=x . Our first plaintext byte 6b combined with key byte 2b yields 40. Do not substitute integer addition or XOR the entire 24/32-byte master key into each round. Expansion differs by more than round count Split the master key into four-byte words w[0]…w[Nk−1]. For each later index i, start with t=w[i−1]: 1. At multiples of Nk, rotate t left by one byte (RotWord), substitute its bytes (SubWord), then XOR Rcon[i/Nk]. Only AES-256 has another branch: when i mod 8=4, apply SubWord alone, with no rotation or Rcon. Otherwise keep t unchanged. In all cases set w[i]=w[i−Nk] XOR t . Rcon is a four-byte word whose first byte takes 01,02,04,08,10,20,40,80,1b,36 , generated by field doubling. Round r uses w[4r]…w[4r+3]. AES-192’s six-word expansion cycle therefore crosses four-word round-key boundaries; it does not supply a six-word round key. For our AES-128 key, w[0]=2b7e1516 and w[3]=09cf4f3c. RotWord gives cf4f3c09; SubWord gives 8a84eb01; XOR with 01000000 gives 8b84eb01. Therefore w[4]= 2b7e1516 XOR 8b84eb01=a0fafe17 . Continuing gives round key one, a0fafe1788542cb123a339392a6c7605 . This expansion is also checked against FIPS 197 Appendix A. Complete encryption and inversion order Begin encryption with AddRoundKey. Rounds 1…Nr−1 perform SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey. Round Nr performs SubBytes, ShiftRows, AddRoundKey. The initial key addition is not another complete substitution round: ten rounds and eleven round-key groups are consistent. The direct inverse begins with the last round key. Then process ordinary rounds backwards: InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, AddRoundKey, InvMixColumns. Finish with InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes and the original round key. Omitting final-round MixColumns does not eliminate inverse mixing from decryption; ordinary rounds still need it. An equivalent inverse implementation can transform round keys and reorder operations, but its steps must not be mixed casually with this direct inverse. AES specifies an algorithm that different implementations can compare precisely. The components have different roles: nonlinear substitution, positional/column diffusion and secret key addition. Its designers analyze their combination using approaches such as the wide trail strategy; repeating scrambling many times is not a design explanation. Correctness can be reasoned about layer by layer: each operation is invertible, expansion determines the round keys, and reversing the sequence recovers the input. Security asks a different question: can an attacker recover a key or distinguish outputs more cheaply than expected under a stated model? Roundtrips, vectors and intermediate-state checks test algorithm implementation, not that security claim. Keeping block length, key length, round count and key-group count separate also makes debugging concrete. A length error, an indexing error and an expansion error leave different first points of failure. A block cipher answers what happens to these sixteen bytes under this key. Handling long messages, counters, authentication and replay requires surrounding constructions. SP 800-38A describes ECB/CBC/CFB/OFB/CTR modes; SP 800-38D defines GCM’s confidentiality/authentication construction. Their input requirements cannot be compressed into the name AES. A specific current example is TLS 1.3 as specified by RFC 9846. Appendix B.4 lists AES-GCM, AES-CCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 suites, showing three layers: primitive, AEAD construction and protocol. RFC 9846 obsoletes RFC 8446. AES-ECB is not one of those TLS 1.3 AEAD suites. Suite-name hashes do not change the AES block length. This article calls an ECB single-block interface only to obtain the same primitive from Node/OpenSSL: exactly one block, padding disabled, no message protocol. It is a testing arrangement, not an application-default recommendation. Full-round AES, reduced-round variants, related-key models and implementations leaking execution information are different targets. NIST IR 8319 is a dated review, not a statement that every AES instance is broken or secure forever. This article invents neither a fixed 126-bit effective strength nor a quantum attack running time. Under one key, equal input blocks give equal output blocks. Independently applying the bare transformation to repeated message blocks leaks equality. Our two equal blocks produce equal ciphertext: a limitation of that construction, not an incorrect AES calculation. GCM nonce reuse under one key undermines confidentiality and authenticity. On portions reusing the same counter keystream, C1=P1 XOR S and C2=P2 XOR S imply C1 XOR C2=P1 XOR P2 . This does not automatically reveal both full plaintexts from ciphertexts alone. Additional recovery depends on what else is known. RFC 5116 §5.1.1 and SP 800-38D Appendix A discuss the danger and its conditions. Length is not secrecy: a published 128-bit test key supplies no operational secret. Deriving keys from passwords, distributing them and storing them are separate tasks. Osvik, Shamir and Tromer’s original research demonstrates leakage of data-dependent lookup patterns through shared caches. Our JavaScript uses tables, branches, copies and observable intermediate states. It promises no constant-time behavior, dependable erasure, physical attack resistance or fault protection. Run it only on public examples. Correct ciphertext does not remove these extra information channels. AES resulted from NIST’s public selection process, initiated in 1997. NIST announced selection of Joan Daemen and Vincent Rijmen’s Rijndael on October 2, 2000. FIPS 197 carries a publication date of November 26, 2001. AES fixes the block length at 128 bits; the broader Rijndael family does not make other block lengths valid AES. The May 9, 2023 FIPS 197 update improved terminology, presentation and key-expansion diagrams without changing the algorithm. An updated document is not a redesigned cipher. This algorithm article explains the mechanism; the related standard entity still needs its own treatment of document versions, scope, constraints and normative relationships. - Wikipedia search entry for AES 高级加密标准. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=AES%20%E9%AB%98%E7%BA%A7%E5%8A%A0%E5%AF%86%E6%A0%87%E5%87%86 - Handbook of Applied Cryptography (Menezes, van Oorschot, Vanstone). https://www.cacr.math.uwaterloo.ca/hac/ Worked example Take one published or standard test vector, record the input, the ordered steps and the byte-exact output, then compare with an independent implementation. items.title: DES: from public standard to an exhaustible block cipher
items.text: Algorithm : Data Encryption Standard (DES 数据加密标准). DES (Data Encryption Standard) is a symmetric block cipher. It transforms a 64-bit plaintext block into a 64-bit ciphertext block using a 64-bit key, of which 56 bits participate in the algorithm and 8 bits are parity bits. Two parties with the same key can encrypt and decrypt; the algorithm is public and confidentiality "depends on the secrecy of the" key. DES is a 16-round Feistel structure. The 64-bit input first passes through the Initial Permutation (IP) and is split into 32-bit halves L₀ and R₀. Round i computes: R_i = L_{i−1} ⊕ f(R_{i−1}, K_i) where K_i is the 48-bit round subkey. After 16 rounds the halves are swapped and the result passes through the Final Permutation (FP). FP is the inverse of IP: applying IP and then FP returns the original block. The round function f does four things: it "expands the 32-bit right half to 48 bits" with the expansion permutation E; XORs the result with the 48-bit subkey; splits it into eight 6-bit groups, each passed through an S-box that outputs 4 bits (32 bits total); and permutes those 32 bits with P. The S-boxes are the only nonlinear part of DES and the main object of differential and linear cryptanalysis. Subkeys come from the key schedule. The 64-bit key first passes through PC-1, which discards the eight parity bits and leaves 56 bits. The result is split into two 28-bit halves, rotated left according to a fixed schedule, and passed through PC-2, which selects 48 bits for that round. Sixteen rounds therefore produce sixteen 48-bit subkeys, 768 bits of subkey material in total. Decryption uses the same hardware or code with the sixteen subkeys in reverse order. The Feistel structure makes every round invertible even though f itself is not one-to-one; this is an engineering property that distinguishes it from a substitution-permutation network. DES was an early publicly published U.S. federal symmetric encryption standard for unclassified government and commercial data. Before it, strong cryptography was largely the concern of military and intelligence organizations; DES put algorithm details, test vectors and implementation requirements into a public standard that banks, vendors and universities could implement and evaluate together. It became one of the starting points for modern block-cipher engineering and public cryptanalysis. DES also makes the life cycle of a standard concrete. An algorithm can be widely deployed and repeatedly reaffirmed, yet still be retired when key space and computing power change. NIST's historical review notes that DES was expected to serve for about 15 years, but remained in federal legacy systems for decades and was only retired in 2005. It created an ecosystem: modes of operation, message authentication, key management, hardware acceleration and validation testing all grew around DES. FIPS 81 defined ECB, CBC, CFB and OFB modes, which later block ciphers inherited. DES is also the background for understanding AES design trade-offs, the 3DES transition and the distinction between block size and key size as security parameters. Typical DES deployments included sensitive but unclassified government data, financial transactions and older network protocols. NIST's history records that DES was adopted by ANSI as X3.92, the Data Encryption Algorithm, for protecting financial information; in retail banking it protected the personal identification numbers (PINs) used in bankcard transactions. It was also adopted by ISO as DEA-1 and appeared widely in cryptographic products of the period. DES is normally used inside a mode of operation, not by itself. ECB encrypts each 64-bit block independently, so identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks. CBC XORs the previous ciphertext block with the current plaintext block, hiding repetition, but it needs an initialization vector and correct padding. CFB and OFB turn the block cipher into a stream-like generator. A mode defines how the block cipher is used; it cannot repair a 56-bit key or a 64-bit block. 3DES/TDEA extends DES by using three DES keys in an encrypt-decrypt-encrypt (EDE) construction. TDEA key-bundle options and modern usage limits belong to the 3DES entity and are not detailed here. FIPS 46-3 recognized TDEA as a federal algorithm in 1999 while demoting single DES to legacy systems only. The nominal DES key space is 2⁵⁶, or 72,057,594,037,927,936 keys. That number looked large in the 1970s, but became searchable as dedicated hardware and distributed computing spread. In 1998 the EFF's Deep Crack machine completed a public DES challenge in less than three days, breaking the previous 39-day record held by a large network of computers. A 56-bit key is not an acceptable security boundary today. At 10⁹ keys per second, exhausting 2⁵⁶ keys takes about 7.21×10⁷ seconds, roughly 834 days or 2.2834 years; at 10¹² keys per second it takes about 20.02 hours. These are arithmetic lower bounds, not measurements that include candidate filtering, key verification or practical parallelism. They show that the problem "is the size of the key space", not the speed of a single implementation. The S-boxes are the nonlinear core of DES. Differential and linear cryptanalysis in the 1990s significantly reduced its theoretical margin. Differential cryptanalysis exploits high-probability relations between plaintext and ciphertext differences; published results for the full 16-round DES require a pool of about 2⁴⁷ chosen plaintexts to obtain about 2³⁶ usable ciphertexts. Linear cryptanalysis exploits linear approximations involving plaintext, ciphertext and key bits; a 1994 experiment used about 2⁴³ known plaintexts against full DES and recovered all 56 key bits in fifty days. These data volumes are already impractical; they show that block-cipher security cannot be explained by key length alone, and that data complexity is not the same as total attack cost. The DES key schedule has structural problems. Four weak keys make all subkeys identical, so encrypting twice returns the plaintext. Twelve semi-weak keys (six pairs) make one key the inverse operation of another. There is also a complementation property: if key K encrypts plaintext P to ciphertext C, then the bitwise complement of K encrypts the bitwise complement of P to the bitwise complement of C. These are properties of the algorithm, not implementation bugs. They do not break DES by themselves and do not change the exhaustion cost for random keys, but implementations must reject these specific keys. A DES block is only 64 bits. In CBC and similar modes, when plaintexts are drawn from a large space, the probability of a repeated ciphertext block becomes significant after about 2³² blocks, roughly 32 GiB of data. The Sweet32 family of attacks exploits such birthday collisions to recover parts of plaintext from long connections. Block size is therefore a security parameter alongside key size: even a longer key would not make a 64-bit block suitable for modern high-volume protocols. FIPS 46-3 was withdrawn in 2005 (the retained texts attest the year; the precise date is unattested in this dossier). NIST SP 800-67 Revision 2 was withdrawn on January 1, 2024, and TDEA is no longer an approved block cipher; the withdrawal notice allows it for decryption, key unwrapping and MAC verification of already-protected data, but not for new encryption protection. DES itself belongs only in legacy systems, historical teaching and compatibility tests; new systems should use AES or another modern algorithm. In the early 1970s the U.S. National Bureau of Standards (NBS) began a symmetric-key algorithm standard for federal agencies and commercial organizations and issued a public call for candidates. It received an algorithm from IBM in 1974; IBM "had recently developed a family of cryptographic algorithms" for financial transaction protection, such as ATMs. NBS used the IBM "algorithm as the basis for its proposed" DES and held public workshops in 1976 to analyze its utility and security. In 1977 NBS issued FIPS 46, making DES a U.S. federal standard. The standardization was controversial. NIST's historical review records that NSA participated in the evaluation and recommended changes, which IBM made; some critics suspected that NSA had deliberately weakened the algorithm or introduced a trapdoor. A second controversy concerned key length: critics argued that 56 effective bits were "too short for long-term security", and Diffie and Hellman published their classic 1977 analysis of DES exhaustion costs. NBS replied that DES was adequate against "practical attack for the anticipated life of the standard" and would be reviewed every five years. DES was reaffirmed in 1983, 1988, 1993 and 1999, and finalized as FIPS 46-3. In 1998 the EFF's dedicated machine completed a public DES challenge in less than three days, sharply reducing the previous 39-day record. FIPS 46-3 was withdrawn in 2005, and the DES era ended. TDEA survived as a transition scheme until it too was withdrawn in 2024. - Wikipedia search entry for DES 数据加密标准. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=DES%20%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E5%8A%A0%E5%AF%86%E6%A0%87%E5%87%86 - Handbook of Applied Cryptography (Menezes, van Oorschot, Vanstone). https://www.cacr.math.uwaterloo.ca/hac/ Worked example Take one published or standard test vector, record the input, the ordered steps and the byte-exact output, then compare with an independent implementation. items.title: Frequency analysis: from letter counts to testable statistical inference
items.text: Attack : Frequency Analysis (频率分析). Frequency analysis first counts symbols in a ciphertext, then compares the result with the known distribution of a candidate language and proposes and tests letter mappings. For a monoalphabetic substitution, if π maps plaintext letters to ciphertext letters, the count of ciphertext symbol y equals the count of plaintext letter π⁻¹(y). The mapping only renames the counts; it does not change their multiset. The basic quantities are counts and relative frequencies. The count f_i is the number of occurrences of symbol i; for a sample of length L, the relative frequency is f_i/L. Unigram statistics look at individual symbols; digram and trigram statistics look at adjacent pairs and triples, such as TH, HE, ER, IN and AN in English. Combination statistics can provide more structure than single letters, but the sample must be long enough and the preprocessing rule must stay fixed. For a text of length L, the index of coincidence (IC) is IC = Σ f_i(f_i − 1) / (L(L − 1)) . It estimates the probability that two letters drawn at random from the text are equal. For 26 equally likely letters the theoretical value is 1/26≈0.03846; for natural English, HAC gives an estimate of about 0.0667. IC does not require knowing the mapping, so it can first indicate whether a text looks monoalphabetic, polyalphabetic or random. The chi-square goodness-of-fit statistic compares observed and expected counts: χ² = Σ (O_i − E_i)² / E_i , where O_i is the observed count and E_i = L·p_i is the expected count under candidate-language frequencies p_i. For 26 letters, with the expected distribution fixed by an external table and no parameters estimated from the sample, the degrees of freedom are 26−1=25. A smaller chi-square means the observed distribution is closer to the expected one. Decrypting under each of the 26 Caesar shifts and choosing the smallest χ² is a common automatic candidate-ranking method. But χ² is not the whole of frequency analysis, and it is not a law that automatically returns the right answer. It depends on assumptions about letter independence, sample length, language and preprocessing. It compares an overall distribution; it does not directly verify digrams, word shapes or meaning. Treating χ² as a synonym for the method hides those conditions. A workable order is: declare the counting unit and preprocessing; count single letters, repeated letters, digrams and trigrams; compare with a candidate language's frequency table and propose mappings; put the hypothesis back into the full text and check word shapes, context and consistency; use several statistics where needed. Every step can produce multiple candidates rather than one unique answer. Natural language is redundant: letters, combinations and words do not occur uniformly. A monoalphabetic substitution preserves that non-uniformity and only renames the symbols. Frequency analysis exploits the fact that the ciphertext still carries statistical structure, not an algebraic weakness in one key. It separates the size of the key space from whether the structure is hidden. A general monoalphabetic substitution has 26! possibilities, far more than the 26 keys of a Caesar cipher; yet an attacker need not enumerate 26!, because language statistics discard many meaningless candidates. This idea later grew into statistical cryptanalysis more generally: find an invariant, then shrink the candidate space. Frequency analysis is also a teaching entry to statistical inference: observe, form a hypothesis, then test it with more evidence rather than declaring an answer from the tallest bar. It also reminds readers that a designer can resist analysis by changing the statistical structure, for example with polyalphabetic substitution, homophonic substitution or larger blocks. Frequency analysis applies to classical monoalphabetic substitution and simple shift ciphers, for analysis and teaching. For a Caesar cipher, because all candidates differ by one global offset, the shape of the distribution is unchanged; the analyst only has to decide which offset best matches the language. For a general monoalphabetic substitution, several letter mappings must be determined together. For a transposition cipher the role is different. Transposition changes letter positions without changing the total count of each letter identity, so unigram frequencies survive. That can help identify the language and nature of the text, but counts alone cannot recover the permutation. HAC uses this as one way to recognize simple transposition. For a polyalphabetic cipher, the same plaintext letter can become different ciphertext letters at different positions, flattening unigram frequencies. Direct comparison with a single-letter table usually fails; the analyst must first estimate the period and then split the text into columns. Kasiski's method and IC autocorrelation are two related but distinct routes; they are not synonyms for frequency analysis but tools for handling polyalphabetic structure. The worked example shows a period-5 Vigenère ciphertext whose global IC is near random while each of the five columns has an IC near English. For modern block ciphers, frequency analysis cannot simply be transferred. With a large block, tabulating every possible block unit is infeasible; HAC explicitly presents large block size as a condition that precludes simple statistical analysis. Modern cipher security arguments and attack models are also much more elaborate than classical monoalphabetic analysis. A frequency is a statistic, not a fixed label attached to each letter. With an insufficient sample or a highly repetitive text, frequency estimates are unstable, and the most frequent letter need not be the most frequent letter of the language. In the 15-letter ZEBRAZEBRAZEBRA , Z, E, B, R and A each occur three times, and IC is 0.1429, well above the English value of 0.0667. This is not because the text is more English; it is because repetition dominates. When chi-square ranks Caesar shifts for this text, the correct key can rank far down the list. The calculation below demonstrates this failure. Frequency tables come from a particular language and corpus. Technical prose, lists of names, abbreviations, code, mixed languages or specially preprocessed text can deviate from a general table. If the language is wrong, the whole comparison is meaningless. Even within English, genre and period change the distribution; HAC labels its Figure 7.5 estimate as coming from 1964 English text. Homophonic substitution uses several symbols for one high-frequency plaintext letter, deliberately flattening the distribution. Polyalphabetic substitution uses different mappings at different positions. Both break the premise that one ciphertext symbol corresponds to one plaintext letter forever. HAC notes that homophonic substitution complicates simple frequency analysis, while sufficient ciphertext may still permit analysis combined with other statistical properties. It is not absolute immunity. Whether text is uppercased, whether spaces remain, whether punctuation is removed and whether accented letters are folded all change counts and sample length. Two apparently identical “letter frequencies” can come from different rules. Any reported result must state the rule, or the numbers are not comparable. Chi-square compares an overall distribution only. Two different shifts can produce similar χ² values; a short text can let a wrong candidate win; and the true distribution can differ systematically from the expected table. Treating the minimum χ² as already broken is overreach. Use χ² to rank candidates, then cross-check with word shapes, digrams, context and known plaintext. The fact that frequency analysis works on classical ciphers does not mean it directly breaks AES or RSA. Modern block-cipher block spaces, round functions and key sizes are different; HAC's note on large blocks preventing statistical analysis is part of this boundary. Frequency analysis can have analogies in side channels, traffic analysis or statistical testing, but those are different attack models and must not be conflated. Al-Kindi's ninth-century Risāla fī Istikhrāj al-muʿammā (the survey prints it "Risalah fi Istikhraj al Mu'amma") is commonly treated as one of the earliest extant treatises on cryptanalysis. The survey of Arabic cryptology consulted for this batch states that al-Kindi counted Arabic letter frequencies in a text of 3,667 letters and then introduced the technique later known as frequency analysis. The same survey identifies the KACST/KFCRI 2003 volume Arabic Origins of Cryptology, Volume One as an edition and study of the treatise. This article reports it as a claim of the cited survey, because the direct object read in this batch was the survey and its citations, not the manuscript itself. HAC's notes attribute part of the modern terminology and IC history to Friedman: a 1920 Riverbank Publication no. 22 discussed cryptanalysis using the index of coincidence, and Friedman coined the term “cryptanalysis” in 1920. Kasiski's method was originally published in 1863. HAC places these methods within a structural comparison of classical ciphers rather than treating them as equivalent techniques. This history shows frequency analysis as a multilingual, centuries-long statistical practice rather than a single invention on one day. This article states only the attributions and dates the sources support; it does not expand a priority dispute into unverified claims. - Wikipedia search entry for 频率分析. https://zh.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?search=%E9%A2%91%E7%8E%87%E5%88%86%E6%9E%90 - Handbook of Applied Cryptography (Menezes, van Oorschot, Vanstone). https://www.cacr.math.uwaterloo.ca/hac/ Formal model and reproduction steps Frequency Analysis: the registered public parameters, key material or randomness, and message are mapped through the stated transformation to an output checked against the registered criterion. The worked example is a structural reproduction, not a new test vector; parameter ranges, standard versions and implementation details remain source-bound.
